Warm light from the upper left, a few sparks drifting up from its crest. Background: a soft wash of warm amber and pale ochre fading to bare cream paper at the edges.

It is a lean four-legged plant creature in a front three-quarter view, body turned toward the viewer. It has no fur: its body is built of overlapping plates of dark walnut bark with pale growth-ring grain. On its chest a seed pod has split open into a husk breastplate, green and glistening inside. Its legs are bundles of twisted pale roots. Two narrow thorny briars of plum-brown wood grow straight up out of its brow, studded with thorns and fresh leaves. Lime leaves sprout from the seams between the bark plates, and split tan seed pods stand along its spine. Two jagged leaf ears, a fern-frond tail curled up behind, amber eyes in a long face of smooth bark. Warm light from the upper left, a few loose thorns in the air. Background: a wash of moss green and bramble plum, fading to cream paper at the edges.

Background: a wash of sandy gold and soft grey-green, fading to cream paper at the edges.

Warrenking.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. Dramatic low-angle view. One single large regal creature sits facing the viewer on a grassy burrow mound in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its crown of blades and below its mound; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a large, heavy living creature sitting on its haunches, chest out, its two broad front legs planted, seen from the front, its silhouette taller than wide. It has no fur, no feathers and no skin: its whole body is sewn together from patchwork panels of thick matted felt in warm grey and slate, joined by bold visible stitched seams of cream thread, a living quilted creature with weight and muscle, not a toy. Its whole body is drawn over in white chalk lines that map branching tunnels and round chambers, the whole warren, from its shoulders down to its feet. Behind its head rises a ring of exactly five flat chalk-white spade blades on felt stalks, like a crown, no wider than its shoulders. Its front feet are wide flat digging spades of porcelain. Its face is a long blunt panel with a stitched seam down the middle and wise dark eyes with a touch of gold. Golden sunset backlight, rim light on the crown. Background: a wash of warm gold, cream and soft slate, fading to cream paper at the edges.

Pecklet.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. One single small creature stands in a shallow stone fountain basin in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its head and below its feet; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a small living creature on two long thin vertical stilt legs of white porcelain, front three-quarter view. It has no feathers: its round body is a living fireplace bellows, two flat stiff rounded boards of slate felt pressed flat against its sides like folded wings, inside the outline of its body, joined by deep pleated folds of oatmeal felt that open and close, with bold visible stitching along every edge. Its short neck is exactly three pleated felt folds, and its head ends in a short tapered nozzle beak of matte unglazed porcelain, a little puff of air coming out of it. Two loose plumes of combed wool on the back of its head. White chalk arrows and swirling wind lines are drawn across its side boards. Round dark eyes. Soft morning light from the upper left, small ripples around its legs. Background: a soft wash of oatmeal, warm grey and pale slate fading to cream paper at the edges.

Galeheron.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. One single tall narrow creature stands still in meadow grass in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its head and below its feet; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a tall, lean living creature on two long thin vertical stilt legs of white porcelain, front three-quarter view, its silhouette tall and narrow. It has no feathers: its body is a large living bellows, two stiff wing-boards of slate felt folded flat against its sides and pointing down, never spread, with deep pleated folds of warm grey felt between them, every edge bound with bold visible stitching; the trailing edge of each wing-board is a thin blade of matte white porcelain lying along its side. Its long neck rises straight up and is an accordion of exactly nine pleated felt folds. Its head ends in a long tapered nozzle beak of white porcelain. Two long plumes of combed wool hang straight down its back. White chalk spirals and wind lines are drawn on its wing-boards. Amber eyes. Fresh light from the upper left, the grass bending in a gust. Background: a soft wash of pale slate, warm grey and oatmeal fading to cream paper at the edges.

Scampit.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. One single small plump creature sits up on a mossy stone in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its tail and below its stone; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a small plump living creature sitting up, front three-quarter view, holding a hazelnut in its forepaws. It has no fur, no feathers and no skin: its whole body is sewn together from patchwork panels of thick matted felt in oatmeal and warm grey, joined by bold visible stitched seams of cream thread, a living quilted creature with weight and muscle, not a toy. Its tail is a long hollow felt stocking, as big as its body, standing straight up behind its back and bending forward over its head, the open top stuffed with seeds, hazelnuts and a bread crust. Down its back run three stitched felt pocket flaps, each closed with a wooden toggle. Its cheeks are two round drawstring pouches, puffed full. White chalk tally marks counting its stores are drawn on its belly. Its face is a flat round felt panel with a stitched seam across it, no snout and no whiskers, with two bright button-dark eyes and two small porcelain front teeth. Porcelain claws. Warm early light from the upper left, a few crumbs on the stone. Background: a soft wash of oatmeal, pale gold and warm grey fading to cream paper at the edges.

Echopup.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. One single small slender creature sits upright on a cobbled step in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its two horn trumpets and below its paws; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a small slender living creature sitting upright on its haunches, facing the viewer. It has no fur, no feathers and no skin: its whole body is sewn together from patchwork panels of thick matted felt in pale oatmeal, with slate grey panels on its face and legs,, joined by bold visible stitched seams of cream thread, a living quilted creature with weight and muscle, not a toy. In place of ears, two large flared trumpets of chalk-white horn stand straight up from its head, close together, each with a spiral groove running down inside like an old hearing horn. Its tail curls up in front of its paws into a third coiled horn whose open bell faces the viewer. White chalk rings ripple outward across its chest like sound waves. A short blunt muzzle with a stitched seam, porcelain claws, large dark eyes. Soft light from the upper left. Background: a soft wash of warm grey, slate and oatmeal fading to cream paper at the edges.

Haulox.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. One single huge four-legged creature stands on all four legs on a dirt road, seen from the front and foreshortened, its silhouette narrow, in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its shoulder yoke and below its hooves; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a huge, heavy four-legged draft beast standing on all four legs, seen from the front, its long body stretching straight back away from the viewer so it is foreshortened; its two front legs and its two hind legs behind them are all visible, all four hooves on the ground; it has no arms and never stands upright. It has no fur, no feathers and no skin: its whole body is sewn together from patchwork panels of thick matted felt in warm grey and slate, joined by bold visible stitched seams of cream thread, a living quilted creature with weight and muscle, not a toy. Its body is a high rounded mound of quilted panels hanging like a heavy blanket. Grown from the top of its shoulders and joined to its body, a flat straight beam of chalk-white horn like a carter's yoke lies across its back, with squared blunt ends, no wider than its body, with two worn hollows on top. Its small head hangs low in front, hidden under a long fringe of felt strips, showing only a wide flat muzzle plate of matte porcelain and two calm dark eyes; it has no horns on its head. Its knees are big wooden thread spools wound with cream yarn, and its hooves are porcelain. White chalk tally strokes in rows of five are drawn on its quilt panels. Warm afternoon light from the upper left, a little road dust at its hooves. Background: a soft wash of warm grey, oatmeal and pale slate fading to cream paper at the edges.

Pocketmouse.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. One single tiny round creature sits on a flat road stone in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its ears and below its stone; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a tiny living creature whose whole round body is a tightly wound ball of cream spun wool yarn, the strands clearly visible, front three-quarter view. A small flat face of pale grey felt is stitched onto the front of the ball with bold stitches, with two bright black bead eyes and fine white whisker fibres. Two large round ears of thin grey felt, dotted with chalk, stand on top. Two tiny front paws with porcelain claws hold the loose end of the yarn, which trails down off the stone like a tail. A dotted white chalk line winds round the yarn ball like a route on a map. Soft light from the upper left, a gentle shadow under the stone. Background: a soft wash of warm grey, cream and pale slate fading to cream paper at the edges.

Mendlark.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. One single small round creature perches on a weathered fence post in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its beak and below its post; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a small round living songbird-shaped creature, front three-quarter view, its beak pointing straight up to the sky in song, its short tail tucked down. It has no feathers: its round body is a plump stitched pincushion of oatmeal and cream felt, its back and crown bristling with dozens of pins with round porcelain heads instead of feathers. Its beak is a long, straight, very thin porcelain darning needle with a small eye near the tip, a cream thread trailing from the eye. Its two wings are flat felt patches sewn onto its sides with bold blanket stitch. White chalk cross-stitches and dashed seam lines are drawn over its breast. Thin legs with porcelain claws, dark eyes. Gentle dawn light from the upper left, a few loose wool fibres drifting. Background: a soft wash of oatmeal, pale gold and warm grey fading to cream paper at the edges.

Hexcrest.caption: Fantasy creature concept painting in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and confident ink linework, a page from an original fantasy bestiary: the creature is plainly an invented species, not a real animal. Dramatic low-angle view. One single noble four-legged creature sits on a low round stone dais, seen from the front, in the exact centre of the wide frame, compact and complete, taking up only the middle half of the width, with wide empty margins of painted paper on the left and right and clear space above its horns and wings and below its dais; nothing touches or crosses any edge. It is a large, noble four-legged beast sitting on its haunches like a great hound, its two front legs straight and together, chest up and head high, seen from the front, its silhouette narrow and taller than wide. It has no fur, no feathers and no skin: its whole body is sewn together from patchwork panels of thick matted felt in cream and chalk white, joined by bold visible stitched seams of cream thread, a living quilted creature with weight and muscle, not a toy. Behind it a pair of great soft felt moth wings rises from its shoulders, closed together straight up like a tall narrow sail, dusty cream with pale chalk eye-spots, no wider than its body, never spread. Exactly six straight chalk-white horns rise from its head, three on each side stacked one above the other, all pointing upward like the points of a crown, no wider than its shoulders. Its long face is the only panel with no seams and no chalk, smooth and completely blank, with calm pale gold eyes. Porcelain hooves. Warm golden backlight from a high window behind it, rim light along the six horns. Background: a soft wash of warm slate, oatmeal and chalk white fading to cream paper at the edges.

Trail Compass.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single brass pocket compass lies open on a smooth flat stone, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view from slightly above, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left glints on its polished brass case and hinged lid. The compass face is plain cream enamel with a slender red-and-blue needle and simple tick marks around the edge, under a domed glass cover that catches a bright highlight. The inside of its open lid is decorated with a small engraved pattern of leaves. A short loop of worn leather cord curls beside it, and a faint trail of small footprints winds across the grass behind it toward distant soft hills. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale sage green with faint blotches of pigment.

Lucky Satchel.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single small leather satchel sits on a wooden table, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lays soft highlights on its worn tan leather. The satchel is round-bottomed and well used, with a curved flap, a brass buckle and a braided shoulder strap that loops beside it. A small charm hangs from the buckle on a red thread: a four-leaf clover pressed inside a round glass bead. The flap is open, and a few sprigs of clover and two smooth round pebbles spill out. A few small golden glints sparkle around the clover charm. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale gold with faint blotches of pigment.

Moss Poultice.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single poultice rests on a small wooden board, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view from slightly above, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lays soft highlights on its surface. The poultice is a soft folded pad of pale linen packed with bright green moss that bulges at the edges, tied in a neat cross with brown twine. Beside it sit a small clay bowl of crushed green herbs with a wooden pestle and a few sprigs of fresh moss and clover. A thin wisp of soothing pale green steam rises from the poultice. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale moss green with faint blotches of pigment.

Clearwater Vial.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single glass vial stands upright on a flat river stone, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the frame from top to bottom. Warm key light from the upper left shines through it and throws a bright, rippling patch of refracted light onto the stone. The vial is a slender, round-bottomed bottle of clear glass with a cork stopper wrapped in thin twine, filled with perfectly clear water that sparkles with a few tiny bubbles. Beside it lies a small sprig of white flowers. A few drops of water glisten on the stone. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale aqua blue with faint blotches of pigment.

Relay Baton.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single relay baton lies diagonally across a patch of short green grass, in the centre of the frame and seen from slightly above, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lays a long highlight along its length. The baton is a smooth cylinder of polished honey-coloured wood, wrapped at both ends with bands of red and blue cloth ribbon whose loose ends flutter in the air. A curved white chalk line runs across the grass beneath it, and two soft footprints are pressed into the grass beside it. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale sky blue with faint blotches of pigment.

Snare Hook.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single long iron hook leans against a weathered wooden post, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the frame from top to bottom. Warm key light from the upper left glints along its dark iron curve. The hook has a long wooden handle bound with leather and ends in a wide, smooth, curved iron crook like a shepherd's hook, with a coil of rope looped around the handle and trailing onto the grassy ground. A small brass ring sits at the joint between the handle and the hook. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale slate blue with faint blotches of pigment.

Drain Brush.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single wide brush floats at a slight angle in the centre of the frame, seen in a three-quarter view, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lights its polished wooden handle. The brush has a short thick handle of dark wood with a brass ferrule and a broad head of soft grey bristles. As it sweeps, it draws a stream of small glowing motes of light in many colours, red, blue, green, yellow and violet, out of the air and into its bristles, where they fade into a soft glow. A few faded grey motes drift away behind it. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale grey with faint blotches of pigment.

Spike Charm.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single charm pendant hangs from a knotted leather cord in the centre of the frame, filling most of the frame from top to bottom. Warm key light from the upper left glints on it. The charm is a sharp, dark iron spike the length of a finger, bound at its top with copper wire and wrapped with two small thorny rose stems and a red bead. Small fierce sparks of orange light glint around its point. Below it, a soft shadow falls on a flat stone. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale amber with faint blotches of pigment.

Bark Shield.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single round shield stands upright, leaning slightly back, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the frame from top to bottom. Warm key light from the upper left lights its rough textured surface. The shield is made of thick layered tree bark in grey and warm brown, its plates overlapping like scales, bound around the rim with a ring of bent green willow and tufts of soft green moss. A small sprig of oak leaves and two acorns are tied at its centre with twine. It stands on a patch of forest floor with fallen leaves. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale moss green with faint blotches of pigment.

Recall Horn.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single curved horn rests on a mossy stone, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lays soft highlights on its smooth surface. The horn is a long, gently spiralling ram's horn of pale cream and honey brown, banded with brass at its mouthpiece and at its wide bell, and hung on a braided leather strap. A few faint rings of pale golden light ripple outward from its bell like a lingering sound, carrying a few drifting leaves back toward it. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale gold with faint blotches of pigment.

Bloom Seed.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single large seed rests on a small mound of dark rich soil, in the centre of the frame and seen from slightly above, filling most of the frame. Warm key light from the upper left lights it, and a soft golden glow comes from within. The seed is the size of a walnut, glossy brown and teardrop shaped, split open down the middle; from the crack bursts a vigorous green sprout that rises in a spiral, unfurling three leaves and ending in a large half-open bud of pink and white petals. Small motes of golden light rise from the seed. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale spring green with faint blotches of pigment.

Unwind Spray.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single glass atomizer bottle stands on a flat stone, slightly left of the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the frame from top to bottom. Warm key light from the upper left glints on its glass. The bottle is round and made of pale violet glass, with a brass nozzle and a soft rubber bulb in a little net of silk thread. From its nozzle a fine mist sprays toward the right and curls into a slowly unwinding spiral of pale lilac and silver droplets, the spiral loosening as it drifts away. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale lavender with faint blotches of pigment.

Dowsing Rod.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single forked dowsing rod floats in mid-air above stony ground, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lights its smooth wood. The rod is a Y-shaped forked branch of pale hazel wood with the bark peeled from its two handles, its single tip dipping downward toward the ground. Beneath the tip, a faint glowing ripple of six small coloured lights, green, red, blue, yellow, terracotta and violet, rises from a crack between the stones. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale ochre with faint blotches of pigment.

Field Guide.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single closed field guide book lies on a mossy log, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view from slightly above, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lays soft highlights on its cover. The book is thick and well travelled, bound in plain green cloth with worn leather corners and a leather strap with a brass buckle; its cover is completely plain. A red ribbon bookmark and a few pressed leaves and feathers stick out from between its pages. A brass magnifying glass with a wooden handle rests beside it. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale forest green with faint blotches of pigment.

Ash Sifter.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single round sieve hovers level in mid-air, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view from slightly above, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lights its wooden rim. The sieve has a bent beech-wood rim and a fine brass wire mesh. Pale grey ash falls through the mesh in soft streams, while left behind on top are several small glowing gems of colour, red, blue, green, yellow, terracotta and violet, gleaming among the remaining cinders. A small heap of ash lies on the ground below. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale ash grey with faint blotches of pigment.

Scrap Ledger.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single battered notebook lies on a wooden table, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view from slightly above, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lays soft highlights on its cover. The ledger is bound in scuffed brown leather and bulges with loose scraps of plain blank paper, a pressed leaf, a feather and a strip of ribbon tucked between its pages, and it is tied shut with a long string wound around it. A stub of pencil and a small brass paper clip lie beside it. Its leather cover is plain and unmarked. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale tan with faint blotches of pigment.

Clean Slate.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single school slate in a wooden frame leans upright against a small stack of smooth stones, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the frame. Warm key light from the upper left glints on its frame. The slate is a dark charcoal-grey board, freshly wiped perfectly clean, with a faint damp sheen and a few soft swirls left by the cloth. A folded white cloth and a single stick of white chalk lie at its foot. A few small sparkles of light drift across its clean surface. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale blue grey with faint blotches of pigment.

Grove Balm.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single round jar of salve sits on a mossy tree root in a sunlit grove, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view from slightly above, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left lights it. The jar is made of glazed green ceramic, its lid set aside, and is filled with a smooth pale green balm with a swirl on top. Around it lie sprigs of fresh herbs, mint, sage and little white chamomile flowers, and a small wooden spatula. A soft halo of pale green light and a few floating leaves rise from the jar. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale leaf green with faint blotches of pigment.

Charge Coil.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single copper coil stands upright on a small wooden base, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the frame. Warm key light from the upper left glints along its wire. The coil is a tight spiral of bright copper wire wound around a short spool of dark wood, with brass caps at both ends. Small arcs of pale yellow-white electricity crackle from its top cap into the air, and six tiny glowing motes of colour, green, red, blue, yellow, terracotta and violet, circle around it. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale butter yellow with faint blotches of pigment.

Jolt Wire.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single taut copper wire stretches across the frame between two short wooden posts, seen in a three-quarter view from slightly above, filling most of the wide frame, over dry grassy ground. Warm key light from the upper left glints along the wire. The posts are weathered grey wood topped with small white ceramic insulators. In the middle of the wire, a bright jagged spark of yellow-white electricity leaps upward and forks into the air, throwing a flash of pale light on the grass below. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale storm grey with faint blotches of pigment.

Static Net.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single fine net is draped across a low wooden frame, in the centre of the frame in a three-quarter view, filling most of the wide frame. Warm key light from the upper left catches its threads. The net is woven from thin silvery cord in a diamond mesh, weighted at the corners with small round brass weights, and its threads shimmer with a faint crackling static: tiny pale blue-white sparks run along the knots and jump between the strands. In the background, a soft wash of warm parchment cream and pale blue grey with faint blotches of pigment.

Smoke Pellet.caption: Painterly storybook illustration in gouache and watercolour on textured cold-press paper, with visible brush strokes, soft wet-edge pigment blooms and fine pencil linework, showing one everyday object from an original fantasy world. A single small clay pellet lies cracked open on flat stone ground in the lower centre of the frame, seen in a three-quarter view, with a large billowing cloud filling most of the wide frame above it. Warm key light from the upper left lights the edges of the smoke.
